title: Marriott engagement and Irma Thomas revival
summary: Booking Irma Thomas with him at the Marriott, the live album, and introducing her to her later husband.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: We went in the Marriott and I, see, they contacted me for the Marriott. And they asked me, who could I get? Did they think I could get Irma? See, because they really just wanted me for it. I said, well, I think, you know, Irma is in California. I said, I think I can get her if I want her. They said, okay, you know, that'd be fine. So I called Stovall. I said, Stovall, because I didn't know how to get in touch with Irma in California. He gave me her number. And I called her and I told her about the job. I said, and I told her they wanted us. She said, well, I'll set everything up. She said, and I'll take the job. So what I did, I said, well, look, I'm going to let you take care of your business and I'll take care of mine. I said, okay, I got my contract. I'm in. You hand me over. And so I gave her the manager of the room of that. And they talked. And Irma went in and I remember making $1,500 a week. And we stayed in there three months, 12 weeks. We broke all records. And you see, okay, we went back again. You know, after 12, I think we went back for 10 weeks. And we're just fantastic. And then, Irma got so popular down here. Well, we was working and then, so I was, I said, well, you ought to move back. She said, I'm going to consider that. But anyway, they contacted her again about coming in. And said, what she did, brought her band from California. She brought somebody, called a gentleman or something. And they stayed in there about three or four weeks. And they cut a loop. They told her, if you can't come back and hear what Tommy originally, we don't want you. Uh-huh. So, we went back again. Yeah. And so, she had this, I forgot her name. The guy was her manager. Well, that didn't, you know, we did well. But she was well on her way then. But really, what set Irma off, you know, from the hi-hat, was 1976, Jazz Festival.
This is when we recorded live.

Okay. That year, man, was, we played for, well, we were the last act, I think that Sunday evening, whatever, and we would start. And boy, we had, it looked like we had a whole New Orleans. Mm-hmm. And if you listen to it, if you listen to the live thing, it was just pure fantastic. And we just literally totally joined up. But this was the thing that started Irma in the direction of where she is right now. Kind of. 1976.

Yeah, she was completely revived that night, 1976. But, and then, when we left, after we came out of the, you know, I introduced her to Emilia at Code 38, because she came over there, and he wanted to know who she was. I said, that's what Irma doing. He said, ma'am, introduce me to her. I said, okay, we're until intermission. And I introduced her the next Sunday. I didn't see her until the next Sunday. She came there with him. And I, he mattered. What she said, she was never really successful until he got in her life. Mm-hmm. That's what she said. So, but I, she was well on our way anyway. You know, because talent, irregardless, she still had talent. She was going to get that. Yeah.
